subject: Archaeology
title: Roman Mining: Stripping Mountains
description: Learn Roman Mining: Stripping Mountains in one minute.

hook.text: Romans used a technique called hushing — releasing reservoirs of water to blast away entire mountainsides for gold.

buildup.text: At Las Médulas in Spain, they carved 300 miles of tunnels and used water pressure to collapse cliff faces.

discovery.text: Pliny the Elder described the technique and called it 'the ruin of mountains.' He was not exaggerating.

twist.text: The environmental damage was staggering. River systems were polluted with sediment for centuries after mining stopped.

climax.text: Las Médulas is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site — a landscape shaped entirely by Roman industrial-scale mining.

punchline.text: Romans strip-mined with water 2,000 years ago.

quiz.question: What was 'hushing' in Roman mining?
options: Using slaves to dig silently to avoid detection by rivals
Releasing reservoirs of water to blast away mountainsides for gold
Heating rock faces with fire then rapidly cooling them to crack ore
